message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 220, "amount_cents": 9480}, {"order_id": 222, "amount_cents": 30660}, {"order_id": 223, "amount_cents": 23129}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before any payouts, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds W2 reported, so I'll start by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches the three refunds W2 reported (orders 220, 222, 223 with the same amounts), so the check passes. Next I need the customer list, so I'll fetch the orders.
The refunds table matches W2's report, so I can proceed. The orders show three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 25415 cents. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance is 30973 cents. Next I need cobalt's net balance to complete the set of customers.
The refunds table matches W2's report, and I have net balances for all three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll record acme's payout of 25415 cents first.

Acme's payout is recorded. I checked the balances against the orders and refunds: birch has no refunds (19628 + 11345 = 30973) and cobalt's refund of 30660 gives 63688 - 30660 = 33028, both matching net_balance. Recording birch next.

Acme (25415) and birch (30973) are recorded, and I've checked cobalt's figure: orders 222 + 225 = 63688, minus refund 222 (30660), gives 33028, which matches net_balance. Recording cobalt's payout now.

All three payouts were recorded successfully. I rechecked each figure against the orders and refunds: acme is (33101-9480)+(24923-23129)=25415, birch is 19628+11345=30973, and cobalt is (36677+27011)-30660=33028. The batch is complete.
